issue_context.title: ansible_mount does not detect ZFS mounts on Linux
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
The setup module does not return info about ZFS mounts in ansible_mounts.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
`lib/ansible/module_utils/facts/hardware/linux.py`

I believe it is caused by the following line, because zfs mount names do not start with slashes:

```python
            if not device.startswith(('/', '\\')) and ':/' not in device or fstype == 'none':
                continue
```

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible --version" between quotes -->

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE

I got this problem too... :frowning_face: 

### My original code (doesn't work w/ ansible 2.9):

``` yaml
- name: 'Re-gather ansible_mounts'
  setup:
    filter: ansible_mounts

- name: "Getting current targets of mounts"
  set_fact:
    current_mounted_targers: "{{ ansible_mounts | map(attribute='mount') | list }}"
```

### I came up with a workaround with `findmnt --real --list -n`:

``` yaml
- name: 'Re-gather ansible_mounts'
  shell:
    argv: [ 'findmnt', '--list', '--real', '-n', '-o', 'TARGET' ]
  register: findmnt_results

- name: "Getting current targets of mounts"
  set_fact:
    current_mounted_targers: "{{ findmnt_results.stdout_lines }}"
  ignore_errors: "{{ ansible_check_mode }}"
```

review_comments: Most of these 'regular' are the reason I added the exclusion in the first place, specially nfs, fuse and cifs, but basically all cluster file systems that use networking to deliver mounts are susceptible.
In the conversation above, it was discussed to include network mounts and than wrap the processing code in timeout operator (granted, that's not in the PR yet).
The problem is that timeouts are useless when a process is stuck in 'blocking' mode in the kernel, which is why we really want to avoid NFS in particular, but most 'network file systems' in general.
In that case, I can just keep the original scope of the PR and enable ZFS (perhaps some of the non-network fuse mounts as well). #24644 could then probably be closed as `won't fix`.
my intention was to allow this but as a toggle, but not by default
I think I'll need some help here. Can you give me an example of such option implementation, so I can do it the right way?
